body: Implemented tasks 1 and 3 of the plan and proved both. Config reads RATE_LIMIT_MAX and RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS, validates them at startup and refuses to boot on a non-integer or anything below 1, naming the offending variable in the refusal. The middleware rejects an over-budget request with 429 and a Retry-After header carrying whole seconds, asserted against a skewed client clock.U+000AU+000ALocked the storage decision: the budget is a Redis token bucket keyed by address, not an in-process sliding window. RFC 001's sketch cannot satisfy restart safety because process memory is lost, and behind more than one instance each instance would hold a separate budget so the effective limit multiplies by the instance count. Sticky routing was rejected because a rebalance silently doubles the limit with nothing failing loudly.U+000AU+000AWrote task 2, the bucket itself, and it is not correct under concurrency. The read-modify-write is three Redis round trips, so two simultaneous requests from one address can both observe the last token and both consume it. The existing burst test fires sequentially and does not catch it; a concurrency harness was added and is currently red, which is the reproduction.U+000AU+000ATask 4, restart safety, is untouched and deliberately so. A restart test over a racy bucket cannot distinguish a restart failure from a concurrency failure, so it is blocked until the bucket is atomic.
